items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: Oh sure, we went to school together and we started together. We played an Italian band at St. Mary's Church, you know?

ctx.x: Did you know Tony Perrini when you were a kid?

Oh sure, we went to school together and we started together. We played an Italian band at St. Mary's Church, you know? Oh yeah. They had an Italian band that used to rehearse in the backyard, had a big room there. In fact, when I first started there I played peclone I see, instead of trombone. I didn't like it. It didn't mean nothing. I couldn't, I mean there was no sense. You couldn't play, you played melody, you would just plump, plump, plump, you know?

items.title: Tony Parenti and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-06-29
items.q: Wasn't Santa Picora on trombone, or?

ctx.x: Henry. I want to get that straight. There's so many out.

Well, Merritt and Henry. No, no. Well, Merritt was a trumpet player. There's only two trombone players. George and... George came, you know, later. But Henry was the... There was two trombones that Ernest Giordina used. And that was Eddie Edwards and Henry Brunas. They were two of the kings down there. It was... You might have heard about Tom Brown, but they could never play with Giordina's band, because Giordina would play stuff out unorthodox. You understand? He played more. Brown would only play what he knew,…
